summary: Stack layers (Apple WWDC26 233): RDMA over Thunderbolt 5 (transport, macOS 26.2+) -> JACCL (Apple collective-comms library, C++ API, "Jack and Angelos' Collective Communication Library") -> MLX / mlx-lm -> mlx_lm.server.

facts.text: Stack layers (Apple WWDC26 233): RDMA over Thunderbolt 5 (transport, macOS 26.2+) -> JACCL (Apple collective-comms library, C++ API, "Jack and Angelos' Collective Communication Library") -> MLX / mlx-lm -> mlx_lm.server.

MLX backends: MPI, ring (TCP sockets, always available, usually faster than MPI), JACCL (RDMA; "necessary for things like tensor parallelism"), NCCL (CUDA). init(backend=) accepts any/ring/jaccl/mpi/nccl.

JACCL needs a FULL MESH (cable between every pair). Ring backend (jaccl-ring / thunderbolt ring) needs only neighbours, so 5+ nodes possible but higher latency; JACCL picks mesh for small latency-bound messages, ring for large bandwidth-bound ones when connected as mesh.
Four Macs fully meshed = 6 cables, 3 TB5 ports used per Mac (TN3205). RDMA cannot route; app must forward over rings.

Tensor parallelism = default in mlx-lm distributed; speeds decode but all-reduces every layer every token, so needs mesh + RDMA. Pipeline parallelism (`--pipeline` flag on mlx_lm commands) splits layers, does not speed single-stream decode, only exchanges activations at stage boundaries; not all models support it.

Launch: `mlx.launch --hostfile hosts.json [--backend jaccl|jaccl-ring] -- /remote/path/to/mlx_lm.chat|mlx_lm.server|mlx_lm.lora ...` run from any machine (e.g. a MacBook); it SSHes to each node. Executable and MLX must exist at the same path on every node; model cached on every node.
Hostfile = JSON array, one entry per node: "ssh" (hostname), "ips" (rank 0 IP reachable by all; others []), "rdma" (list per peer of rdma_enX device, null for self).

`mlx.distributed_config --verbose --hosts h1,h2,.. --backend jaccl|ring --output file.json [--auto-setup] [--env MLX_METAL_FAST_SYNCH=1]` probes TB topology over SSH, builds hostfile; --auto-setup (needs passwordless sudo) disables Thunderbolt Bridge and configures each link for RDMA; without it, prints commands to review.
MLX_METAL_FAST_SYNCH=1 is "critical" for distributed (compute on GPU, comms on CPU); exo exposes EXO_FAST_SYNCH.

Serving: `mlx.launch --hostfile hosts.json --backend jaccl /remote/path/to/mlx_lm.server --model mlx-community/Qwen-3.5-122B-A3B-8bit` shards automatically; distributed also parallelizes prompt processing across nodes.
Python: `group = mx.distributed.init(strict=True, backend="jaccl")`, `sharded_load` from mlx_lm.utils; Swift and C++ (jaccl::init, all_sum) APIs exist.
Data-parallel fine-tuning: mlx_lm.lora under mlx.launch, scale --batch-size by node count.

exo: auto-discovers peers (zenoh replaced libp2p June 2026), dashboard + API on http://localhost:52415, OpenAI/Claude Messages/Responses/Ollama-compatible APIs, topology-aware auto parallel, placement filters (--max-nodes default 4, ring|jaccl, pipeline|tensor), MLX backend; install from source needs `uv sync --extra mlx`.

llama.cpp RPC: `ggml-rpc-server` on each worker (build -DGGML_RPC=ON), `llama-cli/llama-server --rpc host:port,host:port`; splits layers + KV cache proportional to device memory (override --tensor-split); local tensor cache `-c`; README labels it proof-of-concept, fragile and insecure, never on an open network. Optional RDMA transport (PR #26421, merged Aug 2026): negotiated in handshake, falls back to TCP unless both peers support it; connect using the peer's Thunderbolt IP in --rpc; GGML_RPC_NO_RDMA=1 forces TCP; GGML_RPC_DEBUG=1 for logs.
vllm-metal: Ray executor, pipeline parallel across two Macs over TB validated only on Qwen3-0.6B; needs RAY_ENABLE_WINDOWS_OR_OSX_CLUSTER=1; ring ports 32323/32324 (VLLM_METAL_RING_BASE_PORT).
RDMA Verbs limits (TN3205): send/receive only, max 10 UC queue pairs, max message 16,773,120 bytes, 4095 outstanding work requests. IP over TB and RDMA coexist; interfaces rdma_enX map to enX GIDs.
macOS 26.2 (Dec 2025): RDMA over TB5 ships; exo 1.0 and Jeff Geerling's 4x M3 Ultra (1.5 TB, ~$40k) review launch day; ring backend and MPI predate.

2026: JACCL stability patches landed upstream (mlx #3451 race in MeshImpl::all_reduce merged 2026-05-11; #3459 JACCL barrier merged 2026-04-28; #3152 wc_status check still open as of 2026-05-18 over ~10% small all_reduce cost).
Aug 25 2026: llama.cpp RPC gains Apple RDMA transport.
WWDC26 (June 2026): sessions 232 (agents + distributed) and 233 (distributed inference/training with MLX) make mlx.launch/JACCL the official path.

Source of the claim: WWDC26 232: "distributed inference with MLX has seen significant speed-ups: up to three times with four nodes" (no model, baseline or metric given in that session). The quantified evidence is WWDC26 233: Qwen3.6-27B (dense) tensor-parallel on 4x M3 Ultra "nearly three times the token generation rate of a single machine"; separately fine-tuning 180 -> ~600 tok/s ("more than 3x") data-parallel. So 3x = best case, dense mid-size model, 4 nodes, full mesh, RDMA, Apple's own demo. Not general.

Independent data (Geerling via AppleInsider, M3 Ultra, tok/s decode 1/2/4 nodes): exo+RDMA Qwen3-235B 19.5 / 26.2 / 31.9 (1.6x at 4); DeepSeek V3.1 671B 21.1 / 27.8 / 32.5 (1.5x); Kimi K2 Thinking 2-node 21.6, 4-node 28.3. llama.cpp RPC over TCP: Qwen3-235B 20.4 / 17.2 / 15.2 (gets slower); Kimi 2-node 18.5.
exo's own README claims tensor-parallel speedup up to 1.8x on 2 devices and 3.2x on 4 devices (vendor claim, model unspecified); "99% latency reduction". Geerling: latency 300 us -> <50 us with RDMA.

llama.cpp RPC RDMA PR author numbers (M3 Ultra, Qwen3-0.6B layer-parallel, decode tok/s TCP -> RDMA): 2 nodes 115.6 -> 261.3 (2.26x); 3 nodes 101.1 -> 164.2 (1.62x); 4 nodes 87.7 -> 133.5 (1.52x). Even with RDMA the 4-node number is below the 2-node number; tiny model, RPC-call-dominated (via modelfit.io secondary).

Pipeline concurrency (guruswami-ai, Kimi K2.6 q4, M3 Ultras, May 2026): PP2 single-stream 0.152 tok/s, 4 concurrent 0.567 (3.73x aggregate); PP3 0.189 -> 0.498 (2.64x). Pipeline helps aggregate throughput, not single-stream latency.
RDMA bulk transfer (mlx_lm.share): 597 GB in 1:58 = 5.4 GB/s sustained; 3.5-3.8 GB/s file-transfer demo vs rsync 10GbE 100-200 MB/s.

Verdict on the claim: supported as a best-case figure for a dense ~27B model on 4 M3 Ultras; contradicted as a general figure by independent runs of huge MoE models (1.5-1.6x). Apple 232 gives no baseline.

Low-quality source warning: contracollective.com blog (MPI-only, "M5 Ultra", "macOS 16.2", 14.2 tok/s) contradicts primary docs (ring and JACCL exist) and conflicts with released hardware naming; do not use. gkservis case study ("M4 Ultra", 28 tok/s) likewise unverified marketing.

Weights exceed one Mac's RAM: Kimi K2 Thinking (600+ GB), Kimi K2.6 (1T params, ~1 TB at 8-bit; "does not fit on a single M3 Ultra, fits across four", Apple 233), DeepSeek V3.1 671B 8-bit, a 1.6T-parameter DeepSeek model needing >800 GB (Apple 232). Qwen3-235B and 27-122B models fit on one Ultra; distributing them is for speed/prompt processing only.
Apple's demo models: Qwen3.6-27B, Qwen3.5-122B-A3B-8bit (server), Kimi-K2.6.

jaccl errors: `[jaccl] Changing queue pair to RTR failed with errno 22` (most frequent; hits all nodes at once), `Recv failed with errno=2`, errno=60 timeout. Reported on 3x M3 Ultra, macOS 26.3.1, ~10 load/unload cycles per day; can fire after 23 min idle on the next ConnectToGroup; full reboot of all nodes was the only recovery (exo issue 1847, Apr 2026).

Protection-domain exhaustion: `Couldn't allocate protection domain` after ~60 init/teardown cycles; every failed mx.distributed.init() leaks a kernel RDMA PD; reboot-only (mlx #3207, exo #1847). Mitigation: one JACCL session for many operations; cap restart loops.

SIGSEGV in `libthunderboltrdma.dylib tbt_post_recv` via jaccl RingImpl::all_reduce: worker dies silently, exo main process survives holding a 1-node topology; undetected unless /state topology diffed.

Metal command-buffer timeout: `[METAL] Command buffer execution failed: Caused GPU Timeout Error` when send/recv run on the GPU stream (~5 s); workaround stream=mx.cpu for send/recv (mlx discussion 3481; mlx #3142 WONTFIX upstream). Separate ~60 s per-kernel limit caps long-context pipeline prefill: Kimi K2.6 q4 PP2 ~7-8K tokens, PP3 ~5-6K, while single-node mlx_lm.server handled 24K+ (chunked prefill).
Init barrier: use all_sum(mx.ones(10)), not ones(1), after init before p2p ops (single-element does not reliably sync).
`RTR errno 22 (EINVAL)` on every device pair = Thunderbolt Bridge still active.
mlx.launch hides stderr of non-zero ranks ("rank N exited with code 255").
Plain TCP over Thunderbolt under HPL crashed and rebooted two Macs (Geerling).
TB5 has no switch; full mesh limits RDMA clusters to 4 Macs in practice (Mac Studio 5 RDMA-capable ports per Apple, untested per Geerling); ring forwarding for more.
Mixed macOS versions break RDMA discovery; sleep drops Thunderbolt reachability.
Prefill memory is uneven across ranks (first node holds embeddings/KV init) (secondary source, unverified).
llama.cpp RPC over TCP: scales memory, not speed; throughput falls as nodes are added.
exo trust note: developers went quiet for a stretch before 1.0 (Geerling).
3x claim (Apple, one dense model) vs 1.5-1.6x measured on 235B/671B MoE (Geerling) vs exo's own 3.2x claim.
RDMA enablement: Recovery `rdma_ctl enable` (TN3205, exo, MLX docs, llama.cpp README) vs System Settings toggle (WWDC26 233, OS version unstated).
Reliability: Apple presents it as "easy" vs production reports of reboot-only recovery (exo #1847); guruswami-ai says a patch stack (#3451 etc.) removed reboots by May 2026.
modelfit.io says set `GGML_RDMA_DEV` for llama.cpp RDMA; the README says device is chosen automatically by matching GID of the --rpc address. README is primary.
Exact macOS version that moved enablement to System Settings.
